editorial:
Growing up poor in Madras, you meet a self-taught math genius who gets a chance at Cambridge during WWI. The film follows his bond with strict professor Hardy, culture shock, and pressure to prove his ideas. It feels warm, emotional, and inspiring without being too flashy. You get a clear look at genius, faith, and loneliness.

Acting is strong, especially the lead and Hardy; pacing is steady, sometimes slow in middle. Pros: heartfelt story, beautiful settings, moving friendship. Cons: math details can feel heavy, some scenes predictable. Watch if you like true stories and character dramas. Stream in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent Apple TV, or 4K Blu-ray.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, Ramanujan returns to India sick and dies young, but his work survives. Hardy realizes his friend's genius changed mathematics. You see that his ideas live on and his legacy matters more than his short life. It ends on a sad but inspiring note. The movie closes by reminding you that true brilliance can outlast hardship and time.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves true stories, character dramas, and inspiring biographies.
